newsitem.title: UK: S&P expands coverage to add issuer credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P expands coverage to add issuer credit ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it will now systematically assign its "issuer credit ratings' to define each issuer's overall creditworthiness, separate from its ability to repay any individual obligation.

"In addition, S&P will broaden its application of local currency credit ratings in emerging markets, enabling investors ...to directly compare the entities' creditworthiness based in different countries," the agency said in a statement.
S&P said the broad "issuer' classification allowed consistent comparison across the entire universe of borrowers and counterparties that carry S&P ratings.
It said in place of using senior debt ratings as a kind of shorthand, explicit dissemination of these issuer ratings clarified uncertainties raised by the senior debt rating.

"By comparison, issue ratings are assigned to specific instruments, often incorporating an analysis of third-party support, collateral, structure, and other specifics which go beyond, or are in place of, the rating factors in an issuer rating," S&P said.
The agency said distinctions between local and foreign currency issuer ratings were an indication that a country's external debt might have a higher default probability than its internal debt.
A sovereign's repayment risk on foreign currency debt was higher because it required "willingness to generate or obtain the foreign currency necessary to meet obligations", it said.
Foreign and local currency ratings are identical for the vast majority of issuers, notably in the U.S, Japan, Singapore, and eight European nations with AAA foreign currency ratings.

But S&P said distinctions were more apparent for issuers located in lower-rated countries where issuers' foreign currency ratings were often lower than their local currency ratings due to sovereign risk factors.

"Local currency issuer credit ratings in these countries ... may provide a better sense of relative credit quality than foreign currency issuer credit ratings, which are extensively constrained by external payment risks related to the sovereign."
